newsitem.title: cambodia: Cambodia's Hun Sen issues warning to co-premier.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia's Hun Sen issues warning to co-premier.

text.p: Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen on Wednesday issued an ultimatum to his co-premier, telling him he had to choose between working together or siding with the Khmer Rouge guerrilla group.

The warning, which followed fighting overnight in the streets of the capital between security men loyal to the two prime ministers, was expected to put more strain on the already bitter ties between Hun Sen and Prince Norodom Ranariddh.
Two bodyguards from Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party were killed in a heavy 90-minute exchange of automatic weapon fire and rocket-propelled grenades on Tuesday night.
"I don't understand why my partner in the coalition government went to negotiate wth the Khmer Rouge," Hun Sen told reporters while visitng a school outside the capital.

"Now I give you only a few days to decide whether to carry on to work in the coalition government or go to work with the government of Democratic Kampuchea led by Khieu Samphan. This is the betrayal which cannot be accepted."
Hun Sen was apparently referring to Ranariddh's recent revelation tht he had held negotiations with Khieu Samphan, leader of a provisional rebel government.

Ties between the two premiers, who have led a coalition government since 1993 elections, have sunk to a new low over Ranariddh's attempt to strike a deal with Khieu Samphan and bolster his political position in the run-up to elections due next year.

Khieu Samphan, who has long been seen as less tarnished than other Khmer Rouge leaders, was being held hostage by rebel strongman Pol Pot, who fled his base in northern Cambodia last week after slaughtering his defence chief and 11 family members, Ranriddh has said.
The mastermind of the 1975-79 "killing fields" regime, Pol Pot was now said to be on the run after most of his troops deserted him.
Hun Sen has declared that all talks with the Khmer Rouge were illegal and threatened to arrest anyone who conducted talks.
There was no fresh news on Pol Pot's whereabouts on Wednesday, but Ranariddh's security chief, Serey Kosal, said negotiations with Khmer Rouge defectors who broke with Pol Pot were continuing.
Meanwhile the two prime ministers' political parties issued a joint statement condemning the Tuesday night clash and calling on the armed forces to remain calm.

A bipartisan security committee said the fighting was a shameful incident but it did not represent conflict between the two leaders, but only a clash between a small group of bodyguards loyal to the two men.
Hun Sen said earlier that he too did not see the battle as a fight beween him and is co-premier or the two parties.
"It is not a conflict between the parties or Ranariddh and Hun Sen," he told reporters.
A rocket-propelled grenade that exploded in the front yard of U.S. Ambassador Kenneth Quinn's house, shattering his windows, was aimed at his own nearby house, Hun Sen said.
Hun Sen was at his country residence at the time of the clash and said his bodyguards showed restraint.
In Bangkok a government official said on Wednesday that Thai prime mister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh will visit Cambodia this weekend as planned.

Cambodia is due to become a full member of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) in July. ASEAN currently groups Brunei, Indonesia, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and Vietnam.
